**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 05:54
- [USER] User asked about the process for deciding which cities will host the World Athletics Championships.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF) was historically responsible for selecting host cities for the World Athletics Championships.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAAF would solicit bids from interested cities or countries, involving a bidding process with formal proposals detailing venues, accommodation, transportation, security plans, and economic benefits.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A bid evaluation committee would review proposals, assessing venue suitability, financial and logistical feasibility, audience capacity, local cultural context, and revenue potential.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The IAAF council would vote and select the host city based on the bid evaluation committee's recommendations, typically four to six years before the event.
- [USER] User asked why certain cities are repeatedly chosen to host the World Athletics Championships.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested reasons for repeated selection of certain cities include:
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 1) Infrastructure: Cities with existing or invested infrastructure for international events.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 2) Experience: Cities with a history of successfully hosting major international events.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 3) Location: Cities in regions with strong interest in athletics or favorable for international travel.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 4) Reputation: Cities known for hospitality, safety, and accessibility.
- [USER] User asked for examples of cities that have repeatedly hosted the World Athletics Championships.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of cities that have repeatedly hosted include:
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 1) Helsinki, Finland: Hosted in 1983 and 2005, slated to host again in 2022.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 2) London, United Kingdom: Hosted in 1983, 2005, and 2017.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 3) Tokyo, Japan: Hosted in 1991 and 2019, will host again in 2022.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 4) Göteborg, Sweden: Hosted in 1995 and 2006.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 5) Stuttgart, Germany: Hosted in 1993 and 2009.
  - [ASSISTANT_SAID] 6) Rome, Italy: Hosted in 1987 and 1983.
